node_definition.done_when: Read section 21 of crew-observability-truth and its row in the audit report at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/open-sections-already-landed.html. Seven of its eight measures landed. What remains is measure 8, write exclusivity on the review store. Live claims already admit out-of-repository absolute paths (reckon/crew/dispatch.py, the live-claim conflict check). tests/test_review_record_is_one_runs_claim.py dispatches two review nodes in a temporary config home, each declaring the same review record path under the review store as a write path. It asserts that the second dispatch is refused under the existing scope-conflict refusal, naming the first run and the shared record path, and that a different record path for the second is admitted. If the refusal already holds at your base, the test pins it, and you say so in the manifest with the base arm as evidence. If it does not hold, the conflict check in reckon/crew/dispatch.py is extended to compare out-of-repository review-store paths. Existing scope-conflict tests keep passing; grep tests/ for live_conflicts, scope conflict and reviews to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/review-record-is-one-runs-claim.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
